title: Kanjilink: Kanji Lock Screen
shortDescription: Learn Japanese kanji on your lock screen, in a widget and gentle notifications.
fullDescription:
Learn kanji every time you look at your phone.

Kanjilink puts one Japanese kanji where you already look: on your lock screen, in a home-screen widget and in a gentle notification every few hours. Each kanji shows its meaning and its on and kun readings, with romaji, so you can start from zero.

SPACED REPETITION THAT STAYS OUT OF YOUR WAY
• Tap “I know it” and the kanji comes back in a day, then in a few days, then weeks.
• Tap “Again” and it comes back in 10 minutes.
• Kanji you have seen before appear without their meaning first, so you can test yourself before you reveal it.
• You choose how many new kanji a day (3 to 15) and how often a new one appears (every 1 to 6 hours).

ON YOUR LOCK SCREEN
• Kanjilink can set your lock-screen wallpaper to the current kanji, in three styles: Night, Paper or Indigo.
• Answer straight from the notification with “Again” or “I know it”.
• Quiet hours: no notifications at night.

WIDGETS
• A small widget with the kanji, meaning and reading.
• Stretch it wide for the full meaning and both readings.
• Light and dark, following your phone.

JLPT N5 TO N1
• 2,211 kanji ordered by JLPT level and frequency, easiest first.
• JLPT N5 (79 kanji) is free.
• Kanjilink Pro unlocks N4, N3, N2 and N1 with one payment. No subscription.
• Choose Sans (closest to handwriting) or Serif (book style) for the kanji.

PRIVATE BY DESIGN
• No account, no ads, no tracking.
• Your progress stays on your phone.

Kanji meanings and readings come from KANJIDIC2 by the Electronic Dictionary Research and Development Group (CC BY-SA 4.0). JLPT levels follow Jonathan Waller's lists; the JLPT has not published official kanji lists since 2010, so levels are a study guide. Kanjilink is not affiliated with the JLPT.

Privacy policy: https://kanjilink.vplusstudio.app/privacy
